transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Carla Gutierrez (Aperture - Head of ML), Tom Reeves (Aperture Infra), Nora Singh (Aperture Security)
Link shared: https://redwood.app/deck/reserve-eval (referenced)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Aperture is evaluating options for running high-throughput generative features: reserved GPU pools for predictable latency/cost, private deployment options for regulated data, and a burst strategy for unpredictable load. Major concerns: tenant isolation, auditability (audit logs/KMS), integration with internal SSO, and fallback behavior when reserved capacity is saturated.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um it's Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. we also have Liam from our solutions team. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Carla: good thanks. excited to jump in. we've been poking at different ways to move from our prototype on prem to something more production.
[00:00:20] Tom: yes hi, tom here, i'm focused on infra and cost. our execs want a predictable spend for q4.
[00:00:26] Nora: and i'm nora on security, i'll be looking at the compliance pieces.
[00:00:31] Liam: great, quick agenda: understand your traffic profile, isolation needs, private vs hosted constraints, and then we'll walk through how reserved pools + burst works and what a pilot looks like. sound ok?
[00:00:40] Carla: yep. quick context: we run two major features — a summarization API that's synchronous with tight p95 SLA, and a batch reranker for recommendations that is cost-sensitive. current infra is a mix of on-prem GPUs and spot instances, which is spiky.
[00:00:55] Maya: ok, good. high level question — are you evaluating hosted first or is private deployment a hard requirement?
[00:01:02] Carla: preference is hosted for speed, but any customer data that touches PII must remain in our VPC or on premises. so we need a private deployment for certain clients.
[00:01:11] Nora: right — we need keys stored in our KMS, SAML SSO integration, and audit logs retained for 13 months. SOC2 is a must.
[00:01:20] Liam: understood. Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations, and you can pin model versions. We can also offer dedicated reserved pools inside your VPC to satisfy that.
[00:01:33] Tom: how does isolation work? do we get physical GPU isolation or tenant fencing on the same host?
[00:01:39] Liam: you can pick node-level isolation for dedicated pools — effectively no co-tenancy if you reserve whole nodes. our typical config for node isolation is N GPUs per node, with network and storage isolated at the hypervisor level. if you need absolute air-gap, there's our on-prem package.
[00:01:55] Carla: and burst? we have marketing spikes where load goes 10x for a few hours. we can't always commit to huge reserved capacity.
[00:02:03] Maya: yep — reserved pools with burst credits is common. baseline reserved capacity for your 90th percentile load, and then credits to borrow extra on demand. bursts can be routed to lower-cost model variants or to transient non-reserved capacity.
[00:02:15] Tom: curious about failover — if reserved pool is exhausted, what's the fallback order?
[00:02:19] Liam: routing policy is configurable: priority one is reserved pool, then burst credits on dedicated warm pool, then compatible hosted model variants in another region, then finally best-effort shared hosted. you can tune for cost or latency.
[00:02:32] Nora: audit and telemetry — we need token-level logs and request headers for forensic tracing. retention in our S3. is that possible?
[00:02:38] Liam: yes, we can ship audit logs to your S3 or SIEM. there's an audit pipeline that can include per-request metadata — note sometimes auto-transcription of logs might mangle header names, but the full payload is available.
[00:02:51] Carla: ok good. any requirements from our side for the private control plane? e.g., networking or firewall ports?
[00:02:56] Maya: typical: outbound to Redwood control plane on TLS ports for health and management, or in fully air-gapped on-prem setups we hand over a management bundle. we'll share our private deploy checklist.
[00:03:07] Tom: talk real numbers — if we wanted to reserve 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for 24/7 with ability to burst another 16 for 4 hours/day, ballpark cost?
[00:03:17] Maya: i'll send a tailored pricing schedule, but order-of-magnitude, reserved is discounted 30–50% vs on-demand; burst credits priced at higher rate but still cheaper than unmanaged spot churn once you factor ops. i'll include scenarios for 8 reserved + 16 burst in the follow-up.
[00:03:29] Carla: do you support quantized model variants to reduce cost for reranking?
[00:03:33] Liam: yes — we recommend 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants for batch workloads. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching configs based on the workload profile.
[00:03:44] [00:03:44] Tom: what's the expected p95 for short-chat generation at 1024 tokens on reserved nodes?
[00:03:49] Liam: depends on model, but for smaller models we commonly see p95 sub-150ms on dedicated pools with prewarmed KV cache. for larger Llama-family models at 1k tokens you're looking at a few hundred ms p95 — we'll validate in the benchmark.
[00:04:03] Carla: mention of KV cache — we've seen terms like K-V cash in some docs, just flagging transcription oddities.
[00:04:09] Liam: ha yeah transcripts can be weird. we use prefix caching and KV cache to avoid recomputing context.
[00:04:14] Nora: encryption — at rest and in transit is fine, but we need customer KMS to control keys. any bring-your-own-key options?
[00:04:20] Liam: BYOK supported for private and dedicated deployments via KMS/HSM integrations; logs and model artifacts can be encrypted with your keys.
[00:04:27] Tom: how intrusive is the private deploy installer? our infra team wants minimal churn.
[00:04:32] Liam: typical private deploy uses an operator and Helm charts; we can do an outbound-only control plane with tunnels. install time for a standard VPC deploy is a few hours for infra, a day for end-to-end validation. for on-prem it takes longer.
[00:04:44] Carla: ok let's talk SLA — we need 99.9% availability for the reserved pool and p95 latency guarantees, can you do that?
[00:04:51] Maya: we offer SLAs on Dedicated contracts — specifics depend on commitment tier. 99.9% is within reach with multi-node reservation and warm-pool prewarming. SLA exceptions for scheduled maint windows will be in the contract.
[00:05:02] Tom: what about autoscaling? our traffic is unpredictable; can reserved pools autoscale or is that manual?
[00:05:07] Liam: reserved pools can be configured with autoscaling policies and burst caps. you set scaling thresholds — we can prewarm additional nodes when forecasted to hit burst thresholds. there's also manual burst you can trigger.
[00:05:17] Carla: show me the monitoring surface — what do we see in console?
[00:05:20] Maya: per-route token-level cost, latency histograms, model performance dashboards, and tracing hooks. you'll also get an operations feed for errors and allocation events.
[00:05:29] [00:05:29] Tom: is there RBAC integration with our IdP for console access?
[00:05:33] Liam: yep SAML/SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and per-team RBAC controls.
[00:05:38] Nora: our legal will want data processing addendums and a list of subprocessors. is that standard?
[00:05:42] Maya: yes we have a DPA and subprocessors list — i'll attach in the follow-up.
[00:05:47] Carla: curious on rollback and model versioning — need ability to pin to a previous model if a rollout regresses.
[00:05:52] Liam: Redwood supports model pinning and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback policies. you can define rollback triggers based on quality metrics or latency.
[00:06:01] Carla: for the pilot, we want to validate latency for the synchronous summarization and cost per 1M tokens, and a security review.
[00:06:08] Maya: sounds good. proposed pilot: 4-week pilot, reserved 4 GPUs baseline + 8 burstable, run your test corpus for 7 days of simulated traffic, Redwood runs benchmark and we deliver a report plus recommendations.
[00:06:19] Tom: timeline? we want exec approval by mid-july.
[00:06:23] Maya: we can turn pricing and SOW to you by Friday (2026-07-02), benchmark schedule the week of July 6th.
[00:06:30] Nora: i will need the SOC2 report and list of control mappings before we start.
[00:06:33] Maya: Absolutely. I'll attach SOC2, our security whitepaper, and KMS integration guide.
[00:06:38] [00:06:38] Carla: ok quick technical question — do you support colocated disk for model shards on nodes? we've had OOM issues when model memory is constrained.
[00:06:46] Liam: yes, we can provision local NVMe for shards and configure model offload to CPU for cold portions. we also have quantization and sharding support — we'll test the shard strategy in the benchmark.
[00:06:57] Tom: any limitations on model size on dedicated nodes? we have some 70B models.
[00:07:02] Liam: 70B is supported with model parallelism and sharding; we'll validate speed/latency tradeoffs. sometimes larger models benefit more from specialized kernels; we pick kernels at runtime.
[00:07:14] Carla: security — if we use private deploy, will logs ever transit Redwood cloud? we want to avoid that.
[00:07:20] Liam: in private mode logs can be delivered directly to your S3 and we do not persist them in Redwood multitenant storage. metadata for support cases can be shared with your consent.
[00:07:30] Nora: retention policy flexibility? compliance requires 13 months, but we may need different retention for debug vs audit logs.
[00:07:36] Liam: configurable retention windows, and you can set separate sinks for debug vs audit.
[00:07:41] Maya: If you're comfortable, next steps I propose: I'll send pricing/SOW, Liam will propose benchmark plan, Nora will send compliance artifact list, and we'll schedule a 2-hour SE benchmark next week.
[00:07:52] Carla: agreed.
[00:07:53] Tom: agreed.
[00:07:54] Nora: agreed.
[00:07:56] [00:07:56] Liam: one more operational note — warm-pool prewarm can be scheduled to avoid cold-starts during predictable windows like marketing blasts. we also provide an API to trigger manual prewms, uh pre-warm calls.
[00:08:07] Tom: prewms — yeah, got it.
[00:08:10] Maya: ok quick objection handling — cost: some teams ask why not just run everything on our k8s cluster. two answers: operational overhead and latency predictability. we can show comparative cost + ops in the follow-up.
[00:08:22] Carla: teams worry about vendor lockin. can we export models and data if we leave?
[00:08:27] Maya: yes you can export model artifacts and KV caches; private deployments minimize lock-in. we'll include export policy in the SOW.
[00:08:34] [00:08:34] Tom: anything else on networking? we will need IP allowlists and peering.
[00:08:38] Liam: support for VPC peering, private link, and IP allowlists, and we provide a network diagram in the install guide.
[00:08:46] Carla: ok wrapping up — decision factors are predictability of cost, security compliance, and performance for sync summarization.
[00:08:53] Maya: perfect. final quick recap of action items: Maya will send pricing, SOW, SOC2 and DPA; Liam will prepare benchmark plan and install checklist; Nora will send compliance artifact list. We'll tentatively schedule the SE benchmark July 7th.
[00:09:09] [crosstalk]
[00:09:13] Carla: thanks all, this was helpful.
[00:09:16] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week.

Notes and imperfections: transcription contains minor name mis-attributions in places, shorthand like p95/p50 sometimes written as p95/p50 without context. some technical terms transcribed inconsistently (e.g., K-V cash, prewms).

End of transcript.
